description: The false-positive guard for the row. Every read here is legitimately enclosed and MUST check clean: directly in the `repeat` body, in a nested `repeat` (which reports the innermost turn, spec/commands.md:804), in a nested `repeat`'s COUNT (which is evaluated where the inner `repeat` is written, so it reads the OUTER turn — measured, that line runs 1+2+3 times across the three outer turns), and inside an `if`, a `for … in`, and a comprehension body. The `if` and the `for` rest on spec/execution-model.md:664-667, which says every block other than a handler block or a comprehension body "runs as part of the statement that contains it". The comprehension body deliberately does NOT: that passage excludes it, but it excludes it for `return` (which a comprehension answers with `ol-return-in-comprehension`), and says nothing about `repcount`. It rests instead on spec/execution-model.md:671-690, which names exactly two boundaries — a procedure body and a handler block — so a block it does not name inherits; measured, the runtime resolves the `map` line's `repcount` to the enclosing turn, printing [1], [2], [3]. So an implementation that resets enclosure at any block boundary rather than only at the two the spec names goes red here — which matters, because a false positive that teaches learners to ignore diagnostics is worse than a missing one. It also pins the long `repeat ... end repeat` form, which is the spelling spec/commands.md:808-812's own `repcount` example uses. Measured: `execute()` runs this program clean, printing 26 values — so the two stages agree on every read.
